stem.en: A girl is riding her scooter. Its speedometer reading stays the same. Can the scooter be accelerating?

text.en: No. A steady speedometer reading always means zero acceleration.

feedback.en: The speedometer shows only the speed. The velocity can still change if the direction changes.

text.en: Yes, if it changes direction, for example on a turn.

feedback.en: Right. On a turn the direction of the velocity changes, so the scooter accelerates even at a steady speed.

text.en: Only if the road goes downhill.

feedback.en: Going downhill at the same speed reading does not decide it. What matters is whether the direction changes.

explanation.en: A speedometer shows the speed, not the direction. If the scooter goes round a turn at a steady speed, the direction of its velocity changes, so it is accelerating.

hints.en: Velocity has a magnitude and a direction. Which one does the speedometer show?
